en.heading: January: Bible Month builds on the final Bible Week
en.origin: National Bible Month invites people in the Philippines to read and discuss biblical texts in their cultural and religious context, while recognizing that the state must remain neutral in its treatment of different faiths. Proclamation No. 124 was signed on 5 January 2017, creating an annual January observance. It explicitly states that the last week of January is National Bible Week, so the month and its culminating week have different scopes. The presidential text links the initiative to ethical and spiritual education and recognizes previous public attention to Bible Week; it does not declare every day of January a non-working public holiday.
en.promoter: Office of the President and participating educational and faith organizations are identified as leading or participating institutions in implementing the Philippine national observance and its public-awareness activities.
en.purpose: Support reading and reflection on biblical traditions while respecting religious diversity and civic neutrality.

La Proclamazione n. 124, firmata il 5 gennaio 2017, ha istituito gennaio come mese ricorrente e stabilito che l'ultima settimana sia la Settimana nazionale della Bibbia: due periodi distinti. Il testo presidenziale collega l'iniziativa all'educazione etica e spirituale e richiama la precedente Settimana della Bibbia, senza trasformare ogni giorno di gennaio in festività non lavorativa.

en.heading: November: Filipino Values Month grew from a moral recovery programme
en.origin: Filipino Values Month focuses on everyday conduct, community solidarity and reflection on the values people associate with Philippine culture. It is framed as a civic participation campaign rather than a day commemorating a battle or leader. Proclamation No. 479, signed by President Fidel V. Ramos on 7 October 1994, declared November the annual observance and placed it under the Kabisig People Movement. The decree explicitly refers to the Moral Recovery Program announced in Proclamation No. 62 of 1992, separating the earlier campaign from the formal 1994 month-long designation.

en.heading: September: Peace Consciousness Month replaced an earlier week
en.origin: Peace Consciousness Month in the Philippines encourages understanding of nonviolence, reconciliation and the difficult process of addressing armed conflicts and their social causes. Proclamation No. 675 of 20 January 2004 declared every September the national month and superseded Proclamation No. 161 of 2002, which had prescribed a Peace Consciousness Week from 28 February to 6 March. The presidential text referred to several September peace milestones, including the 1996 agreement with the Moro National Liberation Front, and assigned coordination to the presidential peace-process office.

Il decreto richiama eventi di pace avvenuti in settembre, fra cui l'accordo del 1996 con il Moro National Liberation Front, e affida il coordinamento all'ufficio presidenziale per la pace.

en.heading: March: Women’s Role in History Month and overlooked contributions
en.origin: Women's Role in History Month highlights the contributions of Filipino women across social classes, faiths and communities, including work in education, politics, social reform and voluntary organizations. Proclamation No. 227 of 17 March 1988 called for observance throughout March and explicitly cited House Resolution No. 20, which proposed the annual history focus. The National Commission on the Role of Filipino Women was designated secretariat; the month-long historical recognition is not identical to the separate March 8 National Women's Day established by law in 1990.

it.heading: Marzo: il ruolo delle donne nella storia filippina
it.origin: Il Mese del ruolo delle donne nella storia valorizza il contributo delle filippine di diverse classi, fedi e comunità, nell'educazione, nella politica, nella riforma sociale e nel volontariato. La Proclamazione n. 227 del 17 marzo 1988 ha invitato a celebrare l'intero mese e richiamato la Risoluzione n. 20 della Camera, che proponeva l'iniziativa annuale. La Commissione nazionale sul ruolo delle donne fu designata segreteria; il mese storico non coincide con la distinta Giornata nazionale della donna dell'8 marzo, istituita per legge nel 1990.

en.heading: August: a national month for the Filipino language
en.origin: Buwan ng Wikang Pambansa celebrates Filipino as a national language and invites schools, cultural groups and communities to reflect on language, communication and national identity. President Fidel Ramos signed Proclamation No. 1041 on 15 July 1997, establishing annual celebrations for the complete period 1–31 August, not a single national-language day. The proclamation points to earlier constitutional recognition of a national language and to 19 August, the birthday of former President Manuel Quezon, who is often called the Father of the National Language.

en.heading: November: Rice Awareness Month links food and public wellbeing
en.origin: National Rice Awareness Month in the Philippines focuses on the importance of rice for food, farming livelihoods and efforts to address poverty and malnutrition. President Gloria Macapagal-Arroyo signed Proclamation No. 524 on 5 January 2004, aligning the national campaign with the UN's International Year of Rice in 2004 and designating November every year. The decree also notes the November anniversary of the Philippine Rice Research Institute, founded under Executive Order No. 1061 in 1985; this research-institution milestone is not the same event as the new annual month.
